title: Multi-Region Copy Trading: Ordered, Safe Fan-out
summary: Durably accept ordered lead events, then fan them out to many follower accounts.
Use per-lane idempotency, leases, and broker reconciliation for safe at-least-once processing.
Fail over with one execution owner while keeping accepted events replayable and auditable.

sections.title: Scale, Guarantees & Failure Boundaries
points: Support 10,000 lead events per second and 100,000 followers for one lead trader.
Preserve order for each lead while processing different leads in parallel.
Accepted events must survive regional loss and expose current copy status.
Internal delivery is at least once; safe recovery needs idempotency or reliable broker lookup.
speakingNotes: I would start with one immutable sequence for every lead event.
The platform saves an accepted event before success; failed quorum writes return errors.
Events from one lead must keep order, but leads can run independently.
The broker may be slow, rate limited, unavailable, or unclear after timeout.
Internal delivery is at least once, so duplicate work is expected.
One trade needs broker idempotency or reliable lookup to avoid duplicates.

sections.title: Durable Events, Parallel Lanes, Single Ownership
points: Route each lead to a home region with an ordered ledger and cross-region quorum.
Save the lead event and outbox record together before returning success.
Fan out in batches, then process each lead–follower lane independently.
Use broker adapters for rate limits, retries, status lookup, and provider differences.
speakingNotes: I would separate fast acceptance from slow broker execution.
A home region assigns the lead sequence and owns normal processing.
A quorum commit completes before success; the append-only ledger supports audit and replay.
The fan-out service handles large follower lists in small batches.
Each lead and follower pair becomes an independent ordered lane.
Broker adapters hide different APIs and apply per-broker backpressure.

sections.title: Ordered Fan-out and Safe Broker Execution
points: Partition Kafka by leadId; a sequence number defines the required event order.
Create unique, queryable copy intents for every lead event and follower account.
Advance each lane only after execution, rejection, or unsubscribe skip is terminal.
Use a deterministic client order ID so retries describe the same trade.
Put ambiguous timeouts into reconciliation before sending another broker request.
speakingNotes: The API writes the lead event and outbox row in one transaction.
Every event has an immutable ID and a monotonic lead sequence.
Kafka partitions by lead ID, so one lead keeps its order.
Fan-out writes copy intents in batches with a unique business key.
The key is lead event ID plus follower account ID.
An executor waits for the next sequence in each lane.
It sends a deterministic client order ID through the broker adapter.
The status API reads intent states, not worker memory.
A timeout first triggers a broker lookup and reconciliation.

sections.title: Failure Safety, Failover & Reconciliation
points: Crash and redelivery tests prove unique intent keys prevent duplicate internal work.
Timeout handling queries broker history before retrying; unresolved trades stay UNKNOWN.
Unsubscribe writes a sequence fence; later intents skip before broker submission.
Failover grants one region a fencing epoch; ambiguous lanes wait for reconciliation.
Replay and reconciliation repair state while alerts expose lag, failures, and drift.
speakingNotes: I would test duplicate requests, duplicate messages, worker crashes, and lease expiry.
The hardest test is broker acceptance followed by a lost response.
The worker queries the same client ID before any retry.
If supported, it retries with the same ID; otherwise the trade stays UNKNOWN for review.
Unsubscribe records a cutover sequence in durable subscription state.
Already in-flight broker calls may finish, but later calls are skipped.
Failover waits for lease expiry and then issues a higher epoch.
Old workers lose ownership, and fenced state writes are rejected.
The same client ID makes a late old call safe at an idempotent broker.
Replay rebuilds missing intents; reconciliation compares broker and internal records.
I alert on queue lag, UNKNOWN age, broker errors, lease loss, and replication lag.

sections.title: Recommended Guarantee: Durable, Ordered, Recoverable Copying
points: Durable acceptance and batched fan-out handle high event volume and large follower lists.
Per-lane order, idempotency, leases, and reconciliation protect execution through failures.
Brokers without idempotency or lookup support cannot promise exactly once; UNKNOWN needs review.
speakingNotes: My recommendation is durable acceptance with asynchronous copy execution.
Lead ordering stays local, while follower work scales across many workers.
The trade-off is eventual status instead of immediate execution confirmation.
I would never hide an unsupported broker limitation behind a false guarantee.
